# transcripts that no /capture ever caught, and board-add the keepers. The
# upstream twin of curate.ps1 (which files the board downstream).
#
# Built 2026-08-11 at Damon's ask, after the record pass recovered three months
# of dropped keepers. Zero-cost when there is nothing new: capture_scan.py picks
# candidates first, and if the list is empty no model is spawned at all.
#
# Pipeline order (all daily): extract 6:30 -> THIS 7:00 -> curate files it next night.

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
Set-Location -LiteralPath $PSScriptRoot   # Rhea project root -> boots AS Rhea
. (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "automation_common.ps1")

$py     = "C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python313\python.exe"
$log    = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "memory\capture_log.txt"     # MARKERS ONLY -- this script's own voice
$outLog = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "memory\capture_output.txt"  # the headless instance's transcript

# The monitored process no longer writes into the monitor's log (2026-08-20). Rotate any
# mixed-encoding predecessor once, so a marker in this file actually means the script wrote it.
Initialize-MarkerLog -Log $log

Write-Marker -Log $log -Text "=== capture run $(Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm') ==="

# --- zero-token pre-scan: anything to sweep? ---
$cand = & $py -X utf8 (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "memory\capture_scan.py")
$cand = ($cand | Out-String).Trim()
if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($cand)) {
    Write-Marker -Log $log -Text "nothing to sweep."
    exit 0
}
Write-Marker -Log $log -Text "candidates:`r`n$cand"

# --- resolve claude.exe (mirrors curate.ps1) ---
$realBase    = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Packages\Claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc\LocalCache\Roaming\Claude\claude-code"
$reparseBase = Join-Path $env:APPDATA "Claude\claude-code"
$candidates  = @()
foreach ($base in @($realBase, $reparseBase)) {
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $base) {
        $candidates += Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $base -Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
            Sort-Object Name -Descending |
            ForEach-Object { Join-Path $_.FullName 'claude.exe' }
    }
}
$exe = $candidates | Where-Object { Test-Path -LiteralPath $_ } | Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $exe) { Write-Marker -Log $log -Text "ERROR: claude.exe not found."; exit 1 }

# --- spawn headless Rhea with the brief + today's file list ---
$prompt = (Get-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "memory\capture_prompt.md") -Raw)
$prompt += "`n`n## FILES TO SWEEP TODAY`n`n$cand`n"

# Arrival gate skipped BY DESIGN: this brief says "do not run your full boot
# sequence" — seed + brief is the intended footing for the sweep.
$env:RHEA_SKIP_ARRIVAL = "1"
# --model PINNED, not inherited -- see the note in curate.ps1 (Aug 15 2026: one spent
# Fable cap took down all three nightly jobs, because none of them named a model).
# The run now classifies its own failure and retries once on a cheaper model when the
# cause is capacity rather than a fault; the transcript goes to capture_output.txt.
$run = Invoke-HeadlessRhea -Exe $exe -Prompt $prompt `
    -Model "claude-sonnet-5[1m]" `
    -MarkerLog $log -OutputLog $outLog `
    -AddDir "$PSScriptRoot\memory"

# --- verify the effect, not the exit code (lesson of the Aug 3 curator death) ---
$left = & $py -X utf8 (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "memory\capture_scan.py")
$left = ($left | Out-String).Trim()
if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($left)) {
    Write-Marker -Log $log -Text "verify: all candidates marked swept (ran on $($run.ModelUsed))."
} else {
    Write-Marker -Log $log -Text "verify: UNSWEPT candidates remain -- pass did not finish (status: $($run.Status)). Writing Inbox alert."
    $alert = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot ("Inbox\ALERT_capture_failed_" + (Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd') + ".md")
    $tail = (Get-Content -LiteralPath $log -Tail 40) -join "`n"
    $note = Get-StatusNote -Status $run.Status -ModelUsed $run.ModelUsed -Retried $run.Retried
    @"
# Transcript capture pass failed ($(Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm'))

$note

These extracted sessions were due a capture sweep and did not get marked:

``````
$left
``````

Re-run by double-clicking ``capture_pass.bat``, or let the next Rhea session
investigate. Last 40 lines of capture_log.txt:

``````
$tail
``````
"@ | Set-Content -LiteralPath $alert -Encoding utf8
    try { & (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'paddock\notify.ps1') -Title 'Rhea' -Message 'The transcript capture pass failed. Note left in my Inbox.' } catch {}
}

Write-Marker -Log $log -Text "=== capture done $(Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm') ==="

1	# Shared plumbing for the nightly automations (curate.ps1, capture_pass.ps1,
2	# osint\osint_pass.ps1). Dot-source it:  . "$PSScriptRoot\automation_common.ps1"
3	#
4	# Built 2026-08-20. It exists because the three scripts kept failing IDENTICALLY
5	# and getting fixed three times -- the Aug 15 cap death took all three down at
6	# once, because none of them named a model. Two jobs live here and nothing else:
7	#
8	#   1. THE LOG SPLIT. Each script used to pipe the headless instance's whole
9	#      stdout into the SAME file it wrote its own liveness markers to
10	#      (`... | Tee-Object -FilePath $log -Append`) while writing its own lines
11	#      with Add-Content. PS 5.1 defaults those two to DIFFERENT encodings --
12	#      UTF-16 and the system ANSI codepage -- so the mojibake was designed
13	#      behaviour, not drift. Worse than unreadable: on Aug 19 the capture log
14	#      produced two completion lines for one run, 07:52 before 07:06, from a
15	#      script with exactly one writer. A liveness log that returns impossible
16	#      readings is not a liveness log.
17	#
18	#      The structural fault underneath: THE MONITORED PROCESS WAS WRITING INTO
19	#      THE MONITOR'S OWN LOG. A marker line in that file was not evidence the
20	#      script produced it. So now the script's markers go to <name>_log.txt and
21	#      the headless transcript goes to <name>_output.txt, both UTF-8 no-BOM,
22	#      and a marker means what it says.
23	#
24	#   2. CAPPED IS NOT DEAD. Every guard in this house distinguishes "did the
25	#      work" from "found no work"; none of them distinguished "the account is
26	#      out of capacity" from "the job is broken". One exhausted cap could still
27	#      take the whole layer down and the alert would read as a fault. Now the
28	#      run classifies its own failure, retries once on a named cheaper model,
29	#      and the alert says CAPPED when that is what happened.
30	#
31	# Everything here fails toward the caller: no exception escapes these functions
32	# in a way that would kill a pass that would otherwise have finished.
33	
34	# --- UTF-8 without BOM. PS 5.1's -Encoding UTF8 writes a BOM; this doesn't. ---
35	$script:Utf8NoBom = New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($false)
36	
37	function Write-Marker {
38	    <#  One liveness line, appended as UTF-8 no-BOM. This is the ONLY thing that
39	        should ever write to a marker log -- the headless transcript goes
40	        elsewhere. #>
41	    param(
42	        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Log,
43	        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Text
44	    )
45	    try {
46	        [System.IO.File]::AppendAllText($Log, ($Text + "`r`n"), $script:Utf8NoBom)
47	    } catch {
48	        # A failure to log must never fail a pass.
49	        Write-Host "WARN: could not write marker to $Log -- $($_.Exception.Message)"
50	    }
51	}
52	
53	function Initialize-MarkerLog {
54	    <#  Assert the marker log decodes as UTF-8 before appending to it. The old
55	        logs are mixed-encoding and mostly mojibake; rather than tolerate that
56	        forever in the reader, rotate the bad file out ONCE and start clean.
57	        Nothing is deleted -- the old file keeps its history under a new name. #>
58	    param([Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Log)
59	    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Log)) { return }
60	    try {
61	        $bytes = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($Log)
62	        if ($bytes.Length -eq 0) { return }
63	        # Strict decode: throws on any byte sequence that isn't valid UTF-8.
64	        $strict = New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($false, $true)
65	        [void]$strict.GetString($bytes)
66	        # Valid UTF-8, but a UTF-16 file can decode as... nothing; catch the
67	        # obvious BOM case explicitly so it also gets rotated.
68	        if ($bytes.Length -ge 2 -and $bytes[0] -eq 0xFF -and $bytes[1] -eq 0xFE) { throw "utf-16 BOM" }
69	    } catch {
70	        $stamp   = Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd'
71	        $dir     = Split-Path -Parent $Log
72	        $base    = [System.IO.Path]::GetFileNameWithoutExtension($Log)
73	        $rotated = Join-Path $dir "${base}_legacy_$stamp.txt"
74	        try {
75	            Move-Item -LiteralPath $Log -Destination $rotated -Force
76	            Write-Marker -Log $Log -Text "[$(Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm')] Rotated a non-UTF-8 predecessor to $(Split-Path -Leaf $rotated). This file is UTF-8 no-BOM from here on."
77	        } catch {
78	            Write-Host "WARN: could not rotate $Log -- $($_.Exception.Message)"
79	        }
80	    }
81	}
82	
83	function Get-RunFailureKind {
84	    <#  Classify a headless run's output. Returns one of:
85	          ok      -- nothing that looks like a platform failure
86	          capped  -- out of capacity for the model that was asked for
87	          auth    -- credentials, not capacity (the Aug 3 death, eight days invisible)
88	          error   -- something else went wrong loudly
89	        Deliberately conservative: an unrecognised failure is 'error', never 'ok'. #>
90	    param([string]$Output, [int]$ExitCode)
91	    $o = "$Output"
92	    if ($o -match '(?i)(reached your .{0,40}limit|usage limit|rate limit|limit reached|out of (credits?|capacity)|quota (exceeded|exhausted))') { return 'capped' }
93	    if ($o -match '(?i)(failed to authenticate|oauth session expired|not logged in|invalid api key|authentication_error)')                     { return 'auth'   }
94	    if ($ExitCode -ne 0)                                                                                                                       { return 'error'  }
95	    return 'ok'
96	}
97	
98	function Invoke-HeadlessRhea {
99	    <#  Run a headless pass, keep its transcript out of the marker log, and
100	        retry ONCE on a cheaper model if the first attempt was capped.
101	
102	        Returns a hashtable: Status (ok|capped|auth|error), ModelUsed, Retried,
103	        Output. The caller still verifies its own EFFECT-MARKER afterwards --
104	        this function reports what the platform did, never whether the work
105	        landed. Those are different questions and conflating them is how the
106	        Aug 3 curator death stayed invisible for eight days. #>
107	    param(
108	        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Exe,
109	        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Prompt,
110	        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Model,
111	        [string]$FallbackModel = 'claude-haiku-4-5',   # verified live 2026-08-20; 200K window, no [1m] variant exists
112	        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$MarkerLog,
113	        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$OutputLog,
114	        [string]$AddDir
115	    )
116	
117	    $result = @{ Status = 'error'; ModelUsed = $Model; Retried = $false; Output = '' }
118	
119	    # Nested so it disappears with the call, and so it picks up $Exe/$Prompt/$AddDir
120	    # from the enclosing scope. NOT named $args -- that's an automatic variable.
121	    function RunOnce([string]$m) {
122	        $cliArgs = @('-p', $Prompt, '--model', $m, '--permission-mode', 'bypassPermissions')
123	        if ($AddDir) { $cliArgs += @('--add-dir', $AddDir) }
124	        $prevEAP = $ErrorActionPreference
125	        $ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
126	        # [Console]::OutputEncoding governs how PS DECODES the child's stdout; pinned here
127	        # so the transcript's encoding does not depend on the machine's ambient codepage.
128	        # ($OutputEncoding is the other direction and is not the one that matters.)
129	        #
130	        # HONEST PROVENANCE: I added this believing I had caught real mangling in the first
131	        # run's output file. I hadn't -- the replacement characters were my own terminal
132	        # failing to print an em-dash, and the file was correct both before and after.
133	        # Kept anyway, on its own merit: a script whose correctness rides on the ambient
134	        # console codepage is the same fragility the rest of this file exists to remove.
135	        # Recorded because a fix with a false reason attached teaches the next reader a
136	        # bug that never existed.
137	        $prevEnc = [Console]::OutputEncoding
138	        try {
139	            [Console]::OutputEncoding = New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($false)
140	            $out  = (& $Exe @cliArgs 2>&1 | Out-String)
141	            $code = $LASTEXITCODE
142	        } finally {
143	            try { [Console]::OutputEncoding = $prevEnc } catch {}
144	            $ErrorActionPreference = $prevEAP
145	        }
146	        return @{ Out = $out; Code = $code }
147	    }
148	
149	    # The transcript is appended to its OWN file, stamped, so two runs in a day
150	    # are still separable and nothing the model says can impersonate a marker.
151	    $stampHeader = "`r`n===== $Model @ $(Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss') =====`r`n"
152	
153	    $r = RunOnce $Model
154	    try { [System.IO.File]::AppendAllText($OutputLog, $stampHeader + $r.Out, $script:Utf8NoBom) } catch {}
155	    $kind = Get-RunFailureKind -Output $r.Out -ExitCode $r.Code
156	    $result.Output = $r.Out
157	
158	    if ($kind -eq 'capped' -and $FallbackModel) {
159	        Write-Marker -Log $MarkerLog -Text "CAPPED on $Model -- retrying once on $FallbackModel. This is capacity, not a fault."
160	        $r2 = RunOnce $FallbackModel
161	        $hdr2 = "`r`n===== $FallbackModel (cap fallback) @ $(Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss') =====`r`n"
162	        try { [System.IO.File]::AppendAllText($OutputLog, $hdr2 + $r2.Out, $script:Utf8NoBom) } catch {}
163	        $kind2 = Get-RunFailureKind -Output $r2.Out -ExitCode $r2.Code
164	        $result.Retried   = $true
165	        $result.ModelUsed = $FallbackModel
166	        $result.Output    = $r2.Out
167	        $result.Status    = $kind2
168	        if ($kind2 -eq 'ok') {
169	            Write-Marker -Log $MarkerLog -Text "fallback ran clean on $FallbackModel. Output may be thinner than a full pass -- worth a warm look."
170	        } else {
171	            Write-Marker -Log $MarkerLog -Text "fallback ALSO failed ($kind2) on $FallbackModel."
172	            $result.Status = 'capped'   # the originating condition is what the alert should name
173	        }
174	        return $result
175	    }
176	
177	    $result.Status = $kind
178	    if ($kind -ne 'ok') { Write-Marker -Log $MarkerLog -Text "run classified as: $kind (exit $($r.Code))" }
179	    return $result
180	}
181	
182	function Get-StatusNote {
183	    <#  One human sentence for an alert, so a person reading the Inbox note knows
184	        which of the three things happened without opening a log. #>
185	    param([string]$Status, [string]$ModelUsed, [bool]$Retried)
186	    switch ($Status) {
187	        'capped' { return "**CAPPED, not broken.** The account was out of capacity" + $(if ($Retried) { " and the retry on ``$ModelUsed`` did not clear it" } else { "" }) + ". Nothing is wrong with the script -- it will run normally after the cap resets." }
188	        'auth'   { return "**AUTHENTICATION, not capacity.** The headless session could not log in. This is the Aug 3 failure shape; double-click ``Reauthorize Rhea.bat`` on the desktop." }
189	        'ok'     { return "The run completed without a platform error, so the failure is in the work itself rather than in the plumbing." }
190	        default  { return "The run failed for a reason that isn't capacity or credentials. The transcript is in the matching ``*_output.txt``." }
191	    }
192	}
